headline: TMC USA deep-seabed mining application advances through U.S. review process
summary: A live regulatory signal connecting Pacific polymetallic nodules, U.S. permitting, critical minerals, and AI/data-center supply-chain pressure.
linkedinAngle: This is where mineral security, industrial policy, ocean science, and infrastructure risk collide.

headline: NOAA deep-seabed mining resources page updated with active DSHMRA application guidance
summary: NOAA is a key public source for tracking U.S. deep-seabed hard minerals activity, applications, public notices, and filing requirements.
linkedinAngle: Permitting data is infrastructure intelligence. Tracking filings can reveal supply-chain direction before markets price it in.

headline: 24 new deep-sea amphipod species described from the CCZ
summary: New species descriptions show that biodiversity baselines are still forming in the same region targeted for polymetallic nodule extraction.
linkedinAngle: The same mineral frontier is still a biological frontier.

headline: Hundreds of species documented in recent CCZ biodiversity work
summary: A reminder that deep-sea mineral zones are also data-poor ecosystems where species discovery is still ongoing.
linkedinAngle: Before extraction comes visibility. The tracker turns biodiversity baselines into an intelligence layer.

region: Global deep sea with Pacific relevance
headline: Review warns some visible deep-sea mining impacts may last decades
summary: A broad evidence review found that visible impacts on some abyssal plain environments could persist for decades, while uncertainty remains for vents, seamounts, animals, and plume behavior.
linkedinAngle: The core risk is not just damage. It is uncertainty at industrial scale.

headline: BHP CFO says AI demand is increasing investor interest in copper exposure
summary: Copper is a direct physical bottleneck for data-center expansion: power distribution, substations, transformers, boards, heat sinks, and grid modernization.
linkedinAngle: AI demand turns copper from a commodity into an infrastructure-risk signal.

headline: USGS links data centers to large energy and mineral-resource requirements
summary: Data centers require energy, cooling, electrical infrastructure, server hardware, and minerals such as copper and aluminum across the physical stack.
linkedinAngle: The cloud has a mineral footprint.

headline: Polymetallic nodules contain manganese, iron, nickel, copper, cobalt, and rare earth elements
summary: The CCZ is not a single-commodity story. It is a multi-metal deposit system that overlaps with batteries, electronics, defense, grid modernization, and power infrastructure.
linkedinAngle: Serious critical-minerals intelligence maps deposit types, not just metals.
